cards.explanation: The answer is King Zedekiah. The passage says Seraiah went to Babylon with King Zedekiah of Judah in the fourth year of Zedekiah's reign (Jeremiah 51:59). Seraiah is the quartermaster, so I'm guessing he's the one who knows where everything is packed. I'd want him on my team the next time I lose a spatula, friends.

The answer is disaster. The text says Jeremiah wrote on a single scroll about all the disaster that would come upon Babylon (Jeremiah 51:60). That's one serious scroll, friends. Nobody's sending that one as a get-well card.

The answer is False. Jeremiah says, "When you get to Babylon, see that you read all these words aloud…" (Jeremiah 51:61). Seraiah is told to read ALL of it aloud, not keep the words to himself. I'd be asking for a glass of water, bakers.

The answer is that no one will remain there. Seraiah is to say, "O LORD, You have promised to cut off this place so that no one will remain—neither man nor beast." (Jeremiah 51:62). Neither man nor beast. That covers everybody, friends, and it's a heavy line, so I'll just let it sit there a second.
The answer is False. The text says, "Indeed, it will be desolate forever." (Jeremiah 51:62). Not for a season and not for a little while, bakers. Forever is the word used, and it's a heavy one.

The answer is a stone. Jeremiah says, "When you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and cast it into the Euphrates." (Jeremiah 51:63). A scroll with a stone tied to it is not going to float, friends. Even I could figure out where that ends up.

The answer is that it will sink and never rise again. Seraiah is to say, "In the same way Babylon will sink and never rise again…" (Jeremiah 51:64). The scroll with the stone goes down, and the words say Babylon goes down the same way. It's a heavy picture, friends, so I'll keep it simple and let it speak.

The answer is True. Seraiah's last line is "And her people will grow weary." (Jeremiah 51:64). It comes right after the line about Babylon sinking and never rising again, bakers. Then the writer closes with "Here end the words of Jeremiah."
